- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 5 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model exhibits mean reversion bias; adjust forecast toward recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply 2–5% downward correction if sentiment >0.67 over last 5 days.  
- If sentiment turns sharply negative after a spike, model fails to correct; add 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast if sentiment drops below 0.33 after peak.  
- Model underestimates in low-sentiment periods with high volatility; add 1–2% upward adjustment if sentiment <0.33 and price volatility >2% over last 5 days.
